operations.summary: read the command, options and operands a person or a script gave wisent-errors-swift, the Swift package's command line

causes.cause: it names no command, so nothing would run
causes.remedy: add one of {commands}, as in `{example}`

causes.cause: {quoted_command} is not one of its commands
causes.remedy: run one of {commands}, as in `{example}`

causes.cause: {quoted_option} is not one of its options
causes.remedy: drop {quoted_option}, or give one of {options}

causes.cause: {option} takes a value, and it is the last argument
causes.remedy: give {option} its value, as in `{example}`

causes.cause: {option} takes one value and was given {count} times, so which one is meant cannot be read
causes.remedy: give {option} once, as in `{example}`

causes.cause: it needs {option}, and {option} was not given
causes.remedy: add {option}, as in `{example}`

causes.cause: it takes {expected}, and {count} were given
causes.remedy: run it as `wisent-errors-swift {usage}`

causes.cause: {quoted_value} is not one of its values
causes.remedy: give {option} one of {values}

causes.cause: {quoted_value} is not {shape}
causes.remedy: give {option} {shape}, as in `{example}`

operations.summary: read one JSON document a command of wisent-errors-swift was named, and decode it into what the command reads

causes.cause: no file is at that path
causes.remedy: name a file that exists, or write it first; a relative path is read from {cwd}

causes.cause: the path names a directory, not a file
causes.remedy: name the JSON file inside {path}, not the directory

causes.cause: the operating system refused this process the read
causes.remedy: let the user running wisent-errors-swift read it (chmod u+r {path}), or run it as the file's owner

causes.cause: the file is there and may be read, but the operating system stopped the read before its bytes were in hand
causes.remedy: run the command again once the disk or the network share holding {path} answers; `ls -l {path}` shows whether it is still there

causes.cause: the file is not JSON
causes.remedy: write {path} as JSON; `jq . {path}` points at the place it stops parsing

causes.cause: the file is JSON, but not {shape}
causes.remedy: write {path} as {shape}, as in {example}

operations.summary: build one failure envelope from its options, strictly or with the fallback that never refuses, print it and, with --out, write it to a file

causes.cause: the operating system refused to write the file there
causes.remedy: name with --out a file in a directory this user can write, or leave --out out to print the envelope only

operations.summary: read one failure envelope from a JSON file and print it for a person: its rendered line, then its chain of causes
hold one cause, given field by field, to the declaration rules every runtime holds a catalogue to, and show the refusal it says with the values given

causes.cause: it breaks {count} declaration rule(s)
causes.observed: each is a line on stdout; the first: {first}
causes.remedy: correct the fields as each line says, then check the cause again; catalogue/declaration.json states every rule

operations.summary: hold every functionality of a product's `errors list --json` listing, read from a file, to the declaration rules

causes.cause: {count} of its declarations break the declaration rules
causes.observed: {operations} functionalities read; each problem is a line on stdout; the first: {first}
causes.remedy: correct each declaration in the product's catalogue as its line says, then list and check it again

operations.summary: keep a product's telemetry from a terminal, as its app keeps it: its status, the user's answer, a failure to report, the events waiting exactly as they will go, and sending them
open the telemetry section of a product's Settings, the one its app shows, in a window of its own

causes.failed: opening the telemetry settings window of {product}
causes.cause: this process runs outside a logged-in macOS session, so the window server shows it no window
causes.observed: the window server knows no session of user {user} for this process
causes.remedy: run it from a terminal inside the logged-in session of {user}, or set the level from here with `wisent-errors-swift telemetry set <off|errors|usage> --product {product} --app {app}`

operations.summary: file a product's support report from a terminal, as its app's Report a Problem window files it, and read support's answer to every report it filed
find a product's installed command line program, admit it only when its publisher signed it, run it with its output handed on as it comes, and stop its whole process group on SIGTERM or SIGINT

causes.cause: HOME is not set, so neither ~/.local/bin nor ~/.stado/bin can be named
causes.remedy: run it with HOME set to the home directory {name} was installed under

causes.cause: no executable file named {name} is in either place a release installer puts it
causes.remedy: install {name} with its release installer (stado://releases/{name}/<version>/<platform>/install.sh), which places it in {first}

causes.cause: its code signature does not show that the team {team} signed it as {identifier}, so it is not run
causes.remedy: reinstall {name} with its release installer, which places the program its publisher signed, or remove {path}; a program another publisher signs is named with --identifier and --team

causes.cause: the program was found and admitted, but the system could not start it
causes.remedy: correct what the reason names: a --set name must be non-empty and hold no '=', and a program the kernel cannot execute is reinstalled with its release installer

causes.cause: {step} failed, so whether and how the program ended cannot be told
causes.remedy: run it again; `log show --predicate 'subsystem == "com.wisent.WisentProgram"'` shows what the run recorded of its admission

causes.failed: reading the standard input to hand to {name}
causes.cause: the standard input could not be read to its end
causes.remedy: give --stdin an input that can be read to its end, such as a file (< file) or a pipe whose writer closes it
